prompt:
solution.py is meant to implement the specification below, but it contains several defects. One has been reported: `compress([1, 2, 4, 5, 6])` returns "1-2,4-6" instead of "1,2,4-6". Fix that and every other deviation from the specification. Keep the public names and signatures unchanged and do not change behaviour the specification requires.

Specification: Implement `compress(numbers)` and `expand(text)` in solution.py. `compress` takes any iterable of ints, removes duplicates, sorts ascending and writes the numbers as comma-separated items with no spaces: a run of three or more consecutive integers becomes `first-last`, shorter runs are written as single numbers. Negative numbers keep their sign, so the run -3, -2, -1 is written `-3--1`. An empty input gives the empty string. `expand` is the inverse and returns a sorted list without duplicates. It accepts the same syntax and is more lenient: spaces are allowed around commas and around the range dash, a range may have any length of at least one (`4-4` is just 4 and `1-2` is fine), and items may come in any order and may overlap. An empty or whitespace-only string expands to []. `expand` raises ValueError for a descending range such as `5-3`, for an empty item (as in `1,,2` or a leading or trailing comma) and for any item that is not an integer or a range of two integers.
acceptance: only runs of three or more are hyphenated
